blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-performance-1 (The export loads the organization's whole audit log into memory) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-performance-2 (Building the CSV with map/join blocks the single event loop) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The handler runs `SELECT * FROM audit_events WHERE org_id = $1 ORDER BY
created_at`, loads the rows into an array, builds the whole CSV string with
`rows.map(toCsvLine).join("\n")`, and sends it.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: Stream the rows instead of buffering them: read with a server-side cursor (for example `pg-cursor` or `pg-query-stream`) or keyset pages on `(created_at, id)` of a few thousand rows, and write each CSV line to the response as it is read, honouring back-pressure. Memory then stays constant per request instead of growing with the log.
findings.title: The export loads the organization's whole audit log into memory

findings.evidence:
builds the whole CSV string with
`rows.map(toCsvLine).join("\n")`, and sends it.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: Produce the CSV incrementally from the row stream (a Transform stream piped to `res`), so serialization work is spread across ticks and other requests keep being served during an export.
findings.title: Building the CSV with map/join blocks the single event loop

findings.evidence: `GET /admin/audit-events.csv` SHALL return every audit event of the organization as CSV, oldest first.
findings.location: specs/audit-export/spec.md#Requirement: Administrators export the audit log
findings.recommendation: Either state that the response is streamed (so "every event" is delivered without buffering) or add an optional date range (`from`, `to`) and a scenario covering a large log; leave the choice to the author, since a range changes observable behaviour.
findings.title: The requirement mandates an unbounded result with no range

findings.evidence:
The handler runs `SELECT * FROM audit_events WHERE org_id = $1 ORDER BY
created_at`
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: Check with `EXPLAIN` that an index on `audit_events (org_id, created_at)` exists, and add it to the plan (a migration task) if it does not; without it the query scans and sorts the whole table, all organizations included.
findings.title: No index is named for the export's filter and sort

findings.evidence: **Alternatives considered**: none; the code is the simplest.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The export loads every event, then writes the CSV
findings.recommendation: Record the streaming alternative and the reason for the choice, and back it with a measurement of memory and latency on a realistic volume (for example one organization with seven years of events).
findings.title: The approach is chosen without weighing alternatives or measuring
